input_signals.name: Knowledge Capital Solvency Score
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: A distress score built on intangible-adjusted retained earnings and intangible-adjusted earnings coverage of liabilities separates genuine fragility from accounting fragility better than standard solvency ratios.
input_signals.reasoning: Cumulative R&D expensing permanently depresses retained earnings and current income, mechanically pushing innovative firms into the low-Z-score region of standard distress models. Adding back the R&D stock to retained earnings and R&D flow to earnings before scaling by liabilities restores a solvency measure that reflects real repayment capacity. High values identify firms that are solvent in economic terms but classified as distressed by accounting metrics.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ), ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Adjusted Z Composite
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), RATIO(wcap, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A three-channel distress score in which retained earnings and income are restored for expensed knowledge capital, plus an unadjusted liquidity channel, separates accounting distress from genuine fragility better than a two-channel version.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-channel Knowledge Capital Solvency Score was the archive's best cross-sectional signal (t=4.11) but its alpha was modest, suggesting the score still misranks firms whose adjusted solvency is fine yet whose near-term liquidity is not. Adding working capital to assets — the one Altman channel that is not distorted by intangible expensing — should remove genuinely illiquid firms from the long leg and raise the spread's alpha without diluting the FMB slope.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ), sumrank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ), ratio( wcap, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Earnings Innovator
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Genuine financial fragility shows up as volatile profitability, not as a low level of reported profitability; intangible-intensive firms with stable earnings streams carry knowledge capital, whereas intangible-intensive firms with unstable earnings are truly at risk.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal measured distress through levels (leverage, coverage, cash), yet default risk is fundamentally about the volatility of the earnings process relative to obligations, which no prior proposal tested. High R&D combined with low five-year ROA volatility identifies firms whose apparent accounting weakness is a stable investment policy rather than an erratic business. This opens a second-moment distress channel that is nearly orthogonal to the level-based composites.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), neg( vol( ratio( ib, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill Impairment Coverage Risk
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), NEG(RATIO(ib, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquired intangibles are fragile exactly when current earnings do not cover outstanding liabilities, because weak earnings trigger impairment tests that crystallize the loss and tighten covenants.
input_signals.reasoning: The multiplicative goodwill-leverage signal produced a reliable negative alpha (t=-2.96) but no cross-sectional slope, so this version keeps the acquired-intangible fragility channel while switching the distress leg from static leverage to earnings coverage of liabilities and the combination form to SUMRANK. This changes the economic trigger from balance-sheet stock to flow-based impairment risk, and should convert the existing portfolio evidence into cross-sectional evidence as well.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), neg( ratio( ib, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Knowledge Capital Solvency With Intensity
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The mispricing is largest for firms that are simultaneously intangible-intensive and economically solvent once knowledge capital is restored; intensity identifies who is misclassified, adjusted solvency identifies who is genuinely safe.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive shows the R&D-intensity leg drives FF5 alpha (4.7–4.9%) while the adjusted retained-earnings and coverage legs drive the cross-sectional slope (t>4), and no signal has yet carried all three. Combining them additively should retain the FMB slope of the Z-composite while lifting alpha toward the intensity-based signals. This is the direct consolidation test of the two evidence channels the archive has separated.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), sumrank( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ), ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Industry Neutral Intangible Solvency
input_signals.expression: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible intensity and leverage norms are largely industry attributes, so the accounting-versus-genuine distress distinction is meaningful only relative to industry peers; neutralizing industry should sharpen the signal and stabilize the spread portfolio.
input_signals.reasoning: The best signals so far have low Sharpe relative to their alpha, which is the signature of a spread that is long software/biotech and short capital-intensive industries and therefore carries large uncompensated sector risk. Demeaning each leg within industry isolates the firm-specific component of intangible-adjusted solvency and tests whether the existing FMB evidence survives without the industry tilt. It isolates one specific design choice — industry neutralization — on the archive's best-performing formula family.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: add( ind_zscore( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pre Innovation Profit Coverage
input_signals.expression: RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)
input_signals.hypothesis: The correct measure of debt-servicing capacity for an intangible-intensive firm is profit measured before discretionary knowledge investment, since R&D can be cut in a crisis; scaled by total liabilities this ranks true fragility rather than accounting fragility.
input_signals.reasoning: No prior proposal has used gross profitability, the profitability measure least contaminated by intangible expensing, and adding R&D back makes explicit that research spending is discretionary cash rather than a fixed obligation. As a single clean ratio with full coverage it avoids the degenerate distributions that killed the indicator and product-form signals, and it should produce an interpretable, monotone cross-sectional slope. It tests whether the coverage channel works better with a pre-intangible-investment numerator than with net income.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( add( sub( revt, cogs ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt )

input_signals.name: Tax Revealed Solvency Of Innovators
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(txt, lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Tax expense is a hard, cash-verified signal of economic profit that accounting distress metrics miss; an intangible-heavy firm that still books meaningful taxes against its liabilities owns productive knowledge capital rather than being fragile.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal has measured profitability with reported income, which is precisely the number distorted by intangible expensing and loss carryforwards; the tax line is a different, less manipulable observation of the same underlying profitability. Pairing a five-year knowledge-capital stock with tax-to-liabilities creates a separation between innovators generating taxable income and innovators generating only accounting losses. This opens a data channel (txt) untouched by the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ), ratio( txt, lt ) )

input_signals.name: Innovator Solvency Triple Score
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The cleanest separation of accounting from genuine distress combines who is misclassified (R&D intensity), whether accumulated knowledge capital restores the balance sheet (adjusted retained earnings), and whether pre-innovation profit actually covers obligations.
input_signals.reasoning: The current leader pairs intensity with net-income coverage (alpha 4.4%), while the standalone gross-profit-plus-R&D coverage ratio produced a larger alpha (4.7%) with better Sharpe, so substituting the stronger coverage channel into the leading three-leg structure should dominate both. Gross profit is measured before the intangible expensing that creates the distress illusion, making it the economically correct debt-service numerator for this theme. This is the head-to-head consolidation of the archive's two best mechanisms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), sumrank( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ), ratio( add( sub( revt, cogs ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Adjusted Balance Sheet Plus Gross Coverage
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Stock-based (knowledge-capital-restored retained earnings) and flow-based (pre-innovation profit coverage) solvency are the two economically necessary legs; R&D intensity may add only a factor tilt rather than incremental information.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates one design choice against Signal 1 — the presence of the raw intensity leg — so the pair jointly identifies whether the intensity channel contributes genuine mispricing information or merely levers the sector exposure that raises alpha while depressing Sharpe. It is otherwise the direct numerator upgrade of the gen-0 Knowledge Capital Solvency Score, replacing net income with pre-innovation gross profit. Full coverage and a linear rank form keep the cross-sectional slope interpretable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ), ratio( add( sub( revt, cogs ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Post Innovation Profit Coverage
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)
input_signals.hypothesis: If the theme's core claim is right, deducting rather than adding back research spending should weaken predictive power, because the deduction re-imposes exactly the accounting distortion that makes innovators look distressed.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the deliberate mirror of Pre-Innovation Profit Coverage and is the sharpest available test of whether the intangible add-back — not gross profitability per se — is the source of the abnormal return. A materially weaker result confirms the add-back is the active ingredient and justifies pushing the add-back into other channels; a similar result would tell us the coverage effect is generic profitability and would redirect the search. Cheap, full coverage, and highly diagnostic for the remaining generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt )

input_signals.name: Stability Weighted Knowledge Solvency
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)), SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Genuine fragility is the volatility of the earnings process relative to a fixed obligation, so an intangible-intensive firm with restored book equity and a stable earnings stream is safe even with weak reported profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: The earnings-volatility leg produced the archive's single best alpha t-stat (4.09) but a poor Sharpe when paired only with intensity, suggesting it needs a solvency-level anchor to stabilize portfolio composition. Combining the second-moment distress channel with the first-moment adjusted balance sheet tests whether the two are complementary rather than substitutes. This keeps the highest-alpha ingredient in play while addressing its diagnosed weakness.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( neg( vol( ratio( ib, at ), 5 ) ), sumrank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weakest Link Innovator Solvency
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Default is triggered by the binding constraint, so a firm is genuinely safe only if intangible-adjusted earnings coverage and near-term working-capital liquidity are both adequate; the minimum of the two is the economically correct aggregator.
input_signals.reasoning: Every composite so far averages ranks, which lets a strong solvency leg mask a fatal liquidity shortfall — precisely the error that would put genuinely fragile intangible firms in the long leg. The MIN aggregator implements a conjunction without the degenerate zero mass and skewness that ruined the earlier multiplicative signals, and it should improve the long leg's composition and therefore the Sharpe ratio. It tests aggregator structure, a lever the archive has not yet varied.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Triple Constraint Solvency Minimum
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Genuine safety requires a restored balance sheet, adequate earnings coverage, and adequate liquidity simultaneously; failing any one constraint is sufficient for real fragility regardless of the other two.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-leg MIN beat every averaged composite, so the open question is whether conjunction depth continues to help or whether a third binding constraint makes the long leg too restrictive and unstable. Adding the knowledge-capital-restored retained earnings leg — the ingredient behind the archive's best FMB slopes — is the economically motivated third constraint. The result tells us whether to keep deepening conjunctions or stop at two legs in the consolidation phase.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ), min( rank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunction Safety With Intensity Tilt
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Conjunction identifies which firms are genuinely safe, while R&D intensity identifies which safe firms are most likely to be misclassified as distressed by conventional accounting; the mispricing is concentrated where both hold.
input_signals.reasoning: Across the archive the intensity leg has consistently added roughly one percentage point of alpha (3.3%→4.4%, 3.4%→4.7%) whenever appended to a solvency score, and it has never yet been paired with the MIN aggregator. Averaging the conjunction score with intensity preserves the safety screen while tilting the long leg toward firms whose accounting distress is illusory. This is the highest-expected-value consolidation available given the evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( min( rank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) ), ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) )

input_signals.name: Total Brand And Research Capital Solvency
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), RATIO(ADD(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), COALESCE(xad, 0)), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Advertising builds brand capital that is expensed exactly like research, so the accounting-distress illusion extends to advertising-intensive firms and the add-back should include both intangible outlays.
input_signals.reasoning: Every successful signal in the archive has adjusted only for R&D, leaving consumer-facing brand builders — a large group of apparently low-profitability, high-liability firms — unadjusted and therefore misranked. Including advertising in both the intensity leg and the earnings add-back tests whether the mechanism is about research specifically or about expensed intangible investment generally. The answer determines whether the remaining generations should broaden or narrow the intangible definition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), at ), ratio( add( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Maturity Constrained Knowledge Solvency
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: For an intangible-intensive firm the binding constraint is refinancing maturing debt against unpledgeable assets, so rollover exposure belongs inside the conjunction alongside restored book equity and adjusted earnings coverage.
input_signals.reasoning: The rollover leg delivered the archive's highest alpha t-stat (4.31) but no slope when averaged, which is the signature of a variable that matters only when it binds — precisely what the MIN aggregator captures. This substitutes maturity risk for the working-capital leg in the winning triple, so the comparison against Triple Constraint Solvency Minimum cleanly identifies which liquidity concept is the true binding constraint. If the slope holds near 4.5 with alpha rising toward 5.7%, this dominates the current leader.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ), min( rank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Buffered Knowledge Solvency
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash, not accrual working capital, is the survival buffer for research-intensive firms whose current assets are thin and whose spending is a continuous cash outflow.
input_signals.reasoning: The working-capital leg (act−lct) costs roughly two percentage points of coverage and is dominated by receivables and inventory — items that barely exist for the intangible-intensive firms this theme targets — whereas cash-to-liabilities is available for essentially every firm and is the buffer that actually funds R&D through a downturn. This isolates the liquidity-leg definition while restoring coverage from 0.122 toward 0.145. A stable or improved slope with fuller coverage would make the conjunction family more robust rather than merely better fitted.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ), min( rank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), rank( ratio( che, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunction Plus Restored Book Equity
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))), RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Solvency constraints (coverage, liquidity) are binding conditions best combined by conjunction, while the knowledge-capital-restored balance sheet is a graded valuation input best combined additively.
input_signals.reasoning: Triple Constraint put restored retained earnings *inside* the MIN, which raised the slope but trimmed alpha relative to the two-leg version; this variant places the same leg additively outside the conjunction so the pair identifies whether the balance-sheet channel acts as a hard constraint or as a graded signal. Aggregator placement is the one structural lever the archive has not yet resolved, and it plausibly recovers the 5.8% alpha while retaining a slope above 4. It is a targeted structural test, not a cosmetic variant.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( min( rank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) ), ratio( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) )

input_signals.name: Binding Fragility Maximum
input_signals.expression: MAX(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm is genuinely fragile if its worst dimension is bad — either debt vastly exceeds pledgeable assets or profit before knowledge investment fails to cover liabilities — so the maximum of fragility ranks is the correct short-side aggregator.
input_signals.reasoning: Three separate collateral- and goodwill-based short signals produced reliable negative alphas (t between −2.96 and −3.73) but essentially zero FMB slopes, indicating a relationship concentrated in the joint tail rather than monotone in either variable — the exact structure MAX encodes, mirroring the MIN success on the long side. Using tangible-asset-backed leverage and pre-innovation profit coverage keeps the two themes explicitly interacted. If MAX delivers a slope, the framework becomes symmetric and the long-short spread can be built from both ends.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: max( rank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), sub( at, coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( add( sub( revt, cogs ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Four Constraint Innovator Safety
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(che, lt)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: An intangible-intensive firm is genuinely safe only if restored book equity, adjusted earnings coverage, cash buffer, and refinancing exposure are all adequate; the two liquidity constraints are complements, not substitutes, because cash protects against burn while low maturing debt protects against rollover.
input_signals.reasoning: The cash leg and the maturity leg each independently lifted the FMB slope above 4.5 with alphas near 4.7%, so the untested question is whether they capture different failure modes and therefore stack. Conjunction is the only aggregator that has preserved slopes while adding legs, and each additional constraint has so far removed genuinely fragile firms from the long leg rather than merely shrinking it. This is the natural terminal depth test for the winning family.

input_signals.name: Research Inclusive Liquidity Constraint
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), lct)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: For an intangible-intensive firm, next year's research budget is a de facto obligation alongside current liabilities, so the correct liquidity constraint is cash relative to current liabilities plus the R&D commitment.
input_signals.reasoning: Every liquidity leg tested so far treats research spending as free, yet cutting R&D is exactly what destroys the knowledge capital the long leg is supposed to own — so the denominator should include it. This makes the liquidity constraint theme-specific rather than generic, sharpening the separation between innovators who can sustain their programs and those who will be forced to retrench. It isolates the liquidity denominator while holding the rest of the winning triple fixed.

input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))), NEG(MAX(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))))))

Netting the fragility score against the safety score should produce a spread whose short leg is populated by genuinely fragile intangible-heavy borrowers rather than merely low-coverage firms. input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), RANK(RATIO(che, lt))))

Imposing stability as a binding constraint alongside adjusted coverage and cash tests whether the second-moment distress channel behaves like the maturity channel. It is the last unexploited high-alpha ingredient in the archive.

input_signals.name: Deep Fragility Maximum
input_signals.expression: MAX(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), MAX(RANK(RATIO(dlc, act)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm is genuinely fragile if any single dimension fails: an acquired-intangible-dominated balance sheet, heavy maturing debt against current assets, or adjusted earnings that cannot cover liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-leg MAX was the first short-side signal to deliver both a slope (−2.20) and reliable alpha (−4.0%, t=−3.31), mirroring how conjunction depth improved the long side from 3.49 to 4.85. Deepening the fragility aggregator with the goodwill channel (which alone gave fmb −2.28) and rollover exposure should strengthen the slope, using the intangible add-back in the coverage leg so that R&D expensers are not wrongly shorted.
